name: Dark Vinaceous
lede: Dark Vinaceous is a grayish red from Ridgway's 1912 dictionary, its name Latin for wine-colored, and it shares its exact hex with another of our names, Brick rose.

sections.title: Wine-colored, by name
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 dictionary lists Dark Vinaceous at #A46464, plate XXVII, hue 1″, and the ISCC-NBS circular of 1955 files it as "grayish red" [1]. *Vinaceous* comes from the Latin *vinum*, wine, describing the dull reddish color of diluted red wine[1].

In our color graph the exact same hex is also cataloged under [[brick-rose|Brick rose]], two names sharing one identical swatch [1]. The nearest distinct neighbors are [[hydrangea-red|Hydrangea Red]] and [[copper-penny|Copper Penny]], both 5.0 units away [1]. The Munsell notation is 4.2R 4.8/5.8, and the swatch sits with our [[red|red]] family, its gray modifier also pulling it toward [[grey|grey]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 0.46% of 23,781 paintings, 109 of them, as photographed, with the within-painting lens counting 44 [2]. That makes it rarer than 52% of our named colors [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.4% of the 1,674 paintings from that century, 1.9 times the rate its museums would predict [2]. Within a painting it most often sits as an accent, in 50% of its 44 appearances [2]. It is most over-represented in India, 2.6 times the expected rate, 15 of 721 Indian paintings in the archive [2]. The earliest match dates to 1000, 912 years before Ridgway recorded the name, a floor rather than a first [2].
